newsitem.title: UK: Chubb Security says in talks, may get offer.
newsitem.headline: Chubb Security says in talks, may get offer.

text.p: Britain's Chubb Security set off a surge in its share price on Thursday after it confirmed it was in talks that could lead to a recommended offer for the company.
Chubb's share price closed up 82 pence or more than 24 percent higher at a new year's high of 423 pence in a heavy transaction volume that touched nearly 7.3 million.
"Somebody is definitely interested in Chubb's market share which is everywhere," an industry analyst said.

The manufacturer of electronic and physical security services equipment did not give further details but analysts that the bidder was likely to be North American looking to secure Chubb's strong Asian and Australian markets.

"Such an offer, if made, is not expected to exceed a value of 450 pence per share," the firm said in a statement. With around 281.75 million issued shares, the bid is expected to be around 1.3 billion pounds ($2.1 billion).
Nearly 35 percent of Chubb's 1995/96 revenue -- 269.54 million pounds -- came from Asia and Australia. Some 34 percent came from the UK.

"The company has debts of nearly 100 million pounds, so it (the bid) could be slightly north of that figure (1.3 billion)," said another analyst. "At 19 or 20 times (PE), that's a racy multiple," he added.
The global security services market is estimated to be worth 25 billion pounds.
Analysts speculate that Ingersoll Rand may be in the frame -- as it wraps up a 195 million pound takeover of another British company, Newman Tonks Group.
"They would love to expand their business, they have the money...," an analyst with a French investment bank said.
William Holdings was also mentioned by analysts who still remember its failed bid of Racal Electronics in 1991.
Another U.S. suitor could be Republic Industries.
According to Reuters' Security 3000 data, Chubb's return on equity has been estimated at 24.10 percent with its returns on fixed assets pegged at 39.27 percent.
The company's price to earnings ratio stood at 16.27.

Chubb recently consolidated its hold on the Australian market by acquiring the fire protection and building operations unit from James Hardie Industries last year for A$ 220 million and MSS Security for 31 million pounds.

Although Chubb is seen losing a portion of its 1997 profits due to a stronger pound, analysts said Chubb still remained an attractive proposition in a market that shows few signs of weakening in the immediate future.
"It will be a very good vehicle for consolidating in the overall market," an analyst said.
The company is expected to report a turnover of more than 900 million pounds in its year to March 1997, up from 770.3 million in the previous year. ($1=.6128 Pound)
